text: Every resource you've created in this course, by any tool, has ultimately gone through Azure Resource Manager. This lesson looks at ARM's own native way to declare resources, and the cleaner language Microsoft built on top of it to make writing those declarations easier: Bicep.

Azure Resource Manager is the control plane underneath all of Azure. Its native deployment format is the ARM template — JSON, submitted directly to ARM, but genuinely verbose: a small storage account runs to dozens of lines before you even reach the resources array. Bicep compiles down to that exact same ARM JSON, just written in far cleaner, shorter syntax.

Here's a real Bicep block declaring a storage account — a name, a region, a SKU, and two real security settings, minimum TLS version and blocked public access. Compare it to Chapter 2's New-AzStorageAccount cmdlet: both create the same resource through the same ARM API, but the cmdlet is a one-time action, while this is a standing declaration of what should exist.

You deploy a Bicep file with the exact Azure CLI you already learned in Chapter 4 — az deployment group create, pointed at the file instead of a string of individual flags. And az deployment group what-if works on a Bicep file exactly as it does on raw ARM JSON, previewing every change before anything actually deploys.

Bicep isn't only about shorter syntax. The Bicep extension for VS Code gives live IntelliSense and validation against the real ARM schema as you type, catching a typo'd property before deployment ever runs. The Azure Portal can even export a working Bicep file from a resource you already created, a fast way to see real syntax for something you haven't declared by hand yet.

Since 2023, Microsoft has recommended Bicep over hand-written ARM JSON as the default way to author Azure infrastructure, while every ARM capability still carries over underneath. It's Azure-only, and proud of it. Next up: AWS's own native IaC service, which answers the same declarative question with YAML-based stacks instead of Bicep files.
